name: App root component & global state
gap: No root component, by design: every screen reads and writes LKStore directly and re-reads on lk:enter, so there is no global state to hold and nothing to keep in step. A root would be a second place that knows what a screen shows. Reason recorded in store.js.

name: In-progress workout banner
gap: The session shelf (session.js) is mounted above the tab bar on fifteen screens, names the session, counts sets and derives elapsed from the record rather than a local clock.

name: Resume-workout dialog
gap: The shelf is the resume affordance and is always on screen while a session is live; the workout log re-enters a live session on lk:enter and an idle one asks. A modal on mount would interrupt somebody who opened the app to do something else.

name: Mount, ErrorBoundary and CDN fallback
gap: The demo wraps each screen boot in a try/catch with a per-screen retry, and chrome.js now catches anything uncaught after boot with a whole-app panel that says the training is safe before it offers the reload. No CDN fallback: this build loads nothing from a CDN.

name: The sync key set & write timestamping
gap: LKStore.changedAt/changedSince stamp every set and remove, and syncKeys() names the 36 keys a sync carries.

name: Storage layer (`ld` / `sd` / `lkStorageUsage`)
gap: LKStore.usage() reports bytes, keys, share of the practical ceiling and whether the phone is writable.

name: Schema migrations
gap: LKStore.migrate() runs on load with four migrations, each idempotent, recording the version reached.

name: `ErrorBoundary` — whole-app crash screen
gap: chrome.js catches error and unhandledrejection and renders a crash panel that answers what somebody actually wants to know first: nothing logged was lost.

name: Event listeners at a system level (54 `addEventListener` calls)
gap: The shared listeners live in chrome.js, store.js, session.js and theme.js — storage, scroll, resize, visibilitychange, click capture, touchend, pointerup, visualViewport, error and unhandledrejection — one place each, none per screen.

name: Timers at a system level
gap: One interval in the build: the shelf ticks once a second and repaints only when its key changes. Everything else is a bounded setTimeout that clears itself.

name: Style profile (theme) switching
gap: theme.js gives Dark, Light and Match device, applied pre-paint from lk_theme, surviving a reload and themeing every screen and the demo shell.

name: Storage-full recovery
gap: A write that cannot reach the disk is kept for the session, fires lk:storage-full, and raises an on-screen banner; Settings measures usage and warns past 80%.

name: Overlay / portal / scroll-lock infrastructure
gap: Sheets, scrims, Escape and a Tab focus trap were already there; chrome.js now locks the scroller behind any open sheet and restores it to the exact offset. No portal: a shadow root per screen in the demo means a portal would have to leave the root that styles it.

name: Keyboard-aware chrome & zoom lock
gap: chrome.js publishes what the keyboard covers as --lk-kb, the bottom chrome lifts by it and the tab bar hides; double-tap zoom is suppressed over the app own controls only.
